title: Difference Between IB 6 and 7: Close the Gap
summary: Learn the difference between IB 6 and 7, how grade boundaries and markschemes work, and the preparation changes that turn missed marks into a 7.
body_markdown:
The **difference between IB 6 and 7** is usually not a dramatic increase in knowledge. A student earning consistent 6s often understands most of the syllabus but repeatedly loses marks through incomplete answers, weak evaluation, imprecise terminology, hidden working, or poor decisions under time pressure.


Closing the gap requires two steps. Calculate how many weighted marks separate you from the grade 7 boundary, then identify which markscheme requirements you fail to demonstrate consistently. Targeted practice must make those requirements visible even in unfamiliar questions and timed conditions.


### What the difference between an IB 6 and 7 means


IB examiners award **marks** before the IB awards a **grade** . Responses receive marks through analytical markschemes, assessment criteria, or markbands. Component marks are then scaled according to their official weightings and combined into an overall subject total.


That total becomes a grade from **1 to 7** using boundaries for the subject, level, examination session, and sometimes examination variant. The IB's[assessment guidance for students and parents](https://www.ibo.org/contentassets/8ecbee9f96af4db98293b97c133516f5/students-and-parents-amended.pdf) distinguishes the marks earned on assessment tasks from the final grade representing overall performance.


The 6-to-7 gap therefore has two parts:


- **Numerical gap:** the weighted marks between your current total and the lower boundary for a 7.
- **Performance gap:** the missing qualities in your work, such as accuracy, development, synthesis, justification, or effective evaluation.


Both matter. Knowing that you need four more marks does not reveal where they are available. Recognizing that your evaluation is weak is also insufficient unless improving it raises your timed scores.


### IB grade boundaries are not fixed percentages


There is no universal percentage that guarantees a 7. **IB grade boundaries** vary between subjects and examination sessions because assessments differ in difficulty. The IB sets boundaries after marking, considering examiner judgment, grade descriptors, statistical evidence, and the performance of each assessment.


The **6/7 boundary** reflects a judgment about where candidate work begins to demonstrate the qualities associated with the higher grade. It should not be treated as a fixed percentage calculated permanently in advance.


RevisionDojo's published May 2025 tables provide these examples:


Subject and level Grade 6 range Grade 7 lower boundary


English A: Literature HL, TZ2 67-80 81


Economics HL 64-77 78


Economics SL 68-79 80


These are **dated examples** , not predictions. Under the English example, students with totals of 68 and 80 both receive a 6, although one is 13 marks from a 7 and the other is only one mark away.


Use the[RevisionDojo IB Grade Boundaries database](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-boundaries) to examine recent sessions for your exact subject and level. Do not select the lowest historical boundary and assume it will return. Set a practice target several marks above the recent range so that normal variation does not remove your 7.


### Calculate your real distance from a 7


Your subject result is normally based on a **weighted total** , not a simple average of paper percentages. If a component has a raw mark of 40 out of 50 and a weighting of 30%, its scaled contribution is:

Calculate each component in the same way and add the contributions. If the relevant historical grade 7 boundary is 78 and your estimated weighted total is 74, the numerical gap is four marks. If recent boundaries range from 78-80, plan to gain more than four marks rather than relying on the lowest cutoff.


Weighting affects where improvement has the greatest value. Two raw marks on a small component may change the final total less than improvements on a heavily weighted examination. Coursework can still be strategically important because it is developed over time, although all revision must follow school rules and IB academic integrity requirements.


Enter results from several honest, timed attempts into the[IB Grade Calculator](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-calculator) . Treat the output as an estimate because future boundaries are unknown and school marking may not reproduce official standardization exactly.


### How grade 7 work differs from grade 6 work


The IB's official[Diploma Programme grade descriptors](https://ibo.org/contentassets/0b0b7a097ca2498ea50a9e41d9e1d1cf/dp-grade-descriptors-en.pdf) do not define a 7 as flawless. They emphasize thorough understanding, precision, well-developed responses, effective analysis and evaluation, appropriate evidence, and clear communication.


A strong 6 may demonstrate many of these qualities, but less consistently. The distinction is often **consistency plus completion** .


Consistent grade 6 pattern Grade 7 pattern


Understands most content but retains identifiable gaps Integrates knowledge confidently across topics


Uses a valid method with occasional execution errors Executes accurately and checks whether results are reasonable


Analyses evidence but sometimes stops at explanation Extends analysis into evaluation or justified conclusions


Uses relevant but general examples Selects precise evidence and explains its significance


Addresses the topic but misses part of the command Shapes the whole response around the command term


Performs strongly on familiar tasks Transfers knowledge to unfamiliar contexts


Reaches top bands occasionally Reaches top bands repeatedly under timed conditions


Grade 7 students do not necessarily write more. They make a greater proportion of their work relevant, explicit, accurate, and rewardable.


### Markscheme features that commonly decide the gap


### Analytical markschemes


Mathematics and science markschemes often assign credit to separate stages. The official[Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specimen materials](https://ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/university-admission/pdfs/dp-mathematics-analysis-and-approaches-specimen-papers-en.pdf) use concepts such as **M marks** for method, **A marks** for accuracy, **R marks** for reasoning, and follow-through credit when an earlier error is used correctly later.


An unexplained calculator answer may therefore earn less credit than expected. One arithmetic error, however, does not always destroy the question if the method is visible. Students moving from 6 to 7 should show substitutions, maintain consistent notation, include units, avoid premature rounding, and interpret results when required.


### Criteria and markbands


Coursework, oral tasks, investigations, and essays may use criteria or holistic markbands. Under a **best-fit** approach, the work is matched to the descriptor that most accurately represents its overall quality. One excellent feature cannot always compensate for a weak criterion or an undeveloped section.


Highlight the verbs and qualifiers in the top bands, then identify where the draft visibly demonstrates them. If essential reasoning is merely implied, make it explicit without adding irrelevant material or violating academic integrity rules.


Extended responses usually move upward through sustained focus, accurate knowledge, developed analysis, well-chosen evidence, synthesis, and justified conclusions. A grade 6 essay may contain excellent paragraphs but also a descriptive section, generic counterargument, or conclusion that summarizes without reaching a judgment.


### Command terms


**Describe** , **explain** , **compare** , **evaluate** , and **to what extent** demand different responses. Correct subject knowledge cannot earn full credit if it answers the wrong command.


An Economics answer may explain a policy accurately but miss top-band evaluation because it never considers assumptions, stakeholders, time frames, or alternatives. In Biology, identifying a relationship is not the same as explaining its mechanism. In English, naming a technique becomes analysis only when its effect, significance, and relationship to purpose are developed.


### Turn recurring losses into a mark-gain plan


Review three timed papers or substantial sections. For every lost mark, classify the cause instead of writing “careless mistake.”


Error category Typical problem Corrective practice


Knowledge Missing fact, formula, example, or definition Active recall followed by application questions


Interpretation Misreading data, scope, or instructions Annotate givens, restrictions, and command terms


Method Selecting an unsuitable process or structure Practise questions requiring method selection


Accuracy Errors in algebra, units, signs, or terminology Maintain an error log and final checklist


Development Correct point without reasoning or evidence Extend claims using causes, consequences, and evidence


Evaluation Generic limitation or unsupported judgment Compare alternatives and justify the most important factor


Communication Hidden working or unclear structure Reproduce clear model presentation in your own wording


Timing Unfinished sections or poor allocation Use timed blocks with planned stopping points


Count the marks in each category. If 40% of losses come from knowledge, content review is justified. If most come from incomplete explanations, inaccurate execution, or timing, rereading notes will have limited value.


Use the[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) for targeted exam-style practice. Jojo AI can help identify missing markscheme elements, but verify important judgments against authorized IB materials, assessment criteria, and teacher feedback.


### A four-week plan to move from 6 to 7


### Week 1: establish a baseline


Complete a representative timed paper and mark it strictly. Calculate the weighted result, compare it with several applicable boundaries, and identify the two error categories costing the most marks.


### Week 2: repair high-frequency weaknesses


Focus on those two weaknesses. If evaluation is weak, write several short evaluative conclusions instead of repeatedly completing full essays. If mathematical communication is weak, practise complete solutions with every method step, unit, and conclusion shown.


### Week 3: use mixed and unfamiliar practice


Topic drills reveal which method is needed and can create false confidence. Move to mixed sets where you must identify the topic, select an approach, and manage time independently. Retest repaired skills several days later rather than immediately after viewing the solution.


### Week 4: verify improvement under pressure


Complete at least two timed simulations on different days. Improvement is credible only when the marks appear without notes, hints, pauses, or selective marking.[RevisionDojo Mock Exams](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) can support timed rehearsal and question-level review.


Aim for a buffer and a stable range across several attempts. One excellent result demonstrates potential, while repeated results demonstrate readiness.


### Common mistakes when chasing IB top marks


Do not study every topic equally when a narrow group of errors causes most losses. Avoid memorizing markscheme phrases without understanding how to apply them to unfamiliar contexts.


More writing is not automatically better. Every sentence or calculation should contribute knowledge, method, analysis, evidence, reasoning, or judgment. Finally, do not rely on untimed scores, since authentic time pressure can expose different weaknesses. The[RevisionDojo IB resources hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) can support learning, but progress should be tested independently under exam conditions.


### Conclusion


The difference between an IB 6 and 7 is not perfection. It is converting strong understanding into visible, markscheme-aligned credit with greater precision, development, and consistency.


Calculate your weighted gap, classify recurring losses, repair the highest-value weaknesses, and confirm improvement through repeated timed work. RevisionDojo's Grade Calculator, Questionbank, Jojo AI, and Mock Exams can support this cycle of diagnosis, correction, and independent retesting.
